ar-158c435d.stem: In general, what do ligaments connect?
ar-158c435d.explanation: Ligaments are bands of dense connective tissue joining bones together; they support the joint passively. The structure joining muscle to bone is a tendon.

ar-3d9b7532.stem: What is the structure joining muscle to bone called?
ar-3d9b7532.explanation: Tendons transmit muscle force to bone. Bursae are sacs that help tendons glide over bone; menisci and labra are intra-articular fibrocartilaginous structures.

ar-3fe924fa.stem: What type of cartilage usually covers the articular surfaces of synovial joints?
ar-3fe924fa.explanation: In most synovial joints the articular surfaces are covered by smooth hyaline cartilage. In a few joints, such as the temporomandibular and sternoclavicular joints, they are covered by fibrocartilage.

ar-5deb5335.explanation: The synovial membrane lining the inside of the joint capsule produces a slippery fluid rich in hyaluronic acid, which nourishes the cartilage and reduces friction.

ar-968e75e8.stem: What is the movement that decreases the angle between two bones (bending) called?
ar-968e75e8.explanation: Flexion is bending and extension straightening (increasing the angle). Abduction moves away from the midline, adduction towards it, and rotation turns a part about its own axis.

ar-59af87db.stem: What is the movement of raising the arm sideways away from the body called?
ar-59af87db.explanation: Abduction is moving a limb away from the midline of the body; at the shoulder it is produced mainly by supraspinatus and deltoid.

ar-4d1f8034.stem: What is the forearm movement that turns the palm upwards (forwards) called?
ar-4d1f8034.explanation: In supination the palm faces up/forwards, in pronation down/backwards; these movements take place at the radio-ulnar joints. Inversion and eversion are movements of the foot.

ar-d52f46c3.stem: What is the movement that turns the sole of the foot inwards called?
ar-d52f46c3.explanation: In inversion the sole turns inwards, in eversion outwards. These movements take place mainly at the subtalar and transverse tarsal joints; most ankle sprains occur in inversion.

ar-3eb5fefe.stem: Which is the most mobile joint of the body?
ar-3eb5fefe.explanation: The shoulder trades stability for a wide range of movement: the humeral head contacts the shallow glenoid only partly. It is therefore the large joint that dislocates most often.

ar-f3f16261.stem: Which is the largest joint of the body?
ar-f3f16261.explanation: The knee, formed by the femur, tibia and patella, is the largest and most complex synovial joint of the body.

ar-809c1821.stem: Which bones take part in the knee joint?
ar-809c1821.explanation: The knee consists of the tibiofemoral and patellofemoral joints. The fibula does not take part in the knee joint; the superior tibiofibular joint is a separate joint.

ar-e4a2fa9a.stem: Between which bones is the shoulder joint?
ar-e4a2fa9a.explanation: The glenohumeral joint lies between the head of the humerus and the glenoid cavity of the scapula. The clavicle and scapula form the acromioclavicular joint.

ar-aec5db37.stem: What type of joint is the hip joint?
ar-aec5db37.explanation: The hip joint is a ball-and-socket joint between the femoral head and the acetabulum; it moves in three axes and, thanks to its deep socket, is more stable than the shoulder.

ar-55d60eb1.stem: Between which bones is the jaw (temporomandibular) joint?
ar-55d60eb1.explanation: The temporomandibular joint lies between the condyle of the mandible and the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle of the temporal bone; it contains a fibrocartilaginous disc.

ar-1c1cd56a.stem: Between which bones is the pubic symphysis?
ar-1c1cd56a.explanation: The pubic symphysis is the fibrocartilaginous joint joining the two pubic bones in the midline in front; the interpubic disc lies between them.

ar-c9695c99.stem: In which joint are the menisci found?
ar-c9695c99.explanation: The medial and lateral menisci lie between the femoral and tibial condyles in the knee; they improve congruence and distribute load.

options: A small fluid-filled sac lined by synovial membrane between structures that rub together
A fibrocartilaginous disc inside a joint
The outer layer of articular cartilage
A band joining muscle to bone
ar-df324558.explanation: Bursae reduce friction between structures that rub against each other, such as tendon and bone or skin and bone. Their inflammation from repeated pressure or friction is called bursitis.

options: By capillaries from the bone marrow
By diffusion from the synovial fluid
ar-0716071b.explanation: Articular cartilage has no vessels, nerves or perichondrium; nutrients come by diffusion from the synovial fluid. That is why cartilage damage does not heal on its own.

ar-7804f95c.stem: In rheumatoid arthritis, what is the inflammatory tissue that erodes articular cartilage and bone called?
ar-7804f95c.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is chronic inflammation of the synovial membrane; the thickened synovium, called pannus, erodes cartilage and bone. Osteophytes are a sign of osteoarthritis, tophi of gout.

ar-a742a27f.stem: In people who work kneeling, swelling in front of the kneecap is a bursitis of which bursa?
ar-a742a27f.explanation: Prepatellar bursitis ('housemaid's knee') is inflammation of the bursa between the patella and the skin from repeated pressure. Infrapatellar bursitis ('clergyman's knee') lies in front of the tibial tuberosity.

ar-4202eeca.stem: What is the main function of the alar ligaments?
options: To prevent excessive flexion of the head
To press the dens against the anterior arch of the atlas
To limit excessive rotation of the head
To join the posterior arch of the atlas to the occiput
To form the anterior wall of the vertebral canal
ar-4202eeca.explanation: The alar ligaments run from the sides of the dens to the occipital condyles and prevent excessive turning of the head at the atlanto-axial joint. The ligament pressing the dens against the anterior arch is the transverse ligament of the atlas.

ar-4ecc76c5.stem: Why is rotation of the spine limited in the lumbar region?
options: Because the facet joint surfaces lie in the sagittal plane
Because the discs are very thin
Because there is no ligamentum flavum
ar-4ecc76c5.explanation: The orientation of the facet joints determines the type of movement in each region: lumbar facets are sagittal and allow flexion-extension but restrict rotation; thoracic facets lie in the frontal plane and rotation is free.

ar-0ab30723.stem: In which vertebrae are the uncovertebral (Luschka) joints found?
ar-0ab30723.explanation: Uncovertebral joints are cleft-like joints between the uncinate processes on the upper lateral margins of the C3–C7 bodies and the vertebra above; their osteophytes can narrow the intervertebral foramen.

ar-ff6c7a3d.stem: Which ligament prevents backward displacement of the condyle at the jaw joint?
ar-ff6c7a3d.explanation: The lateral ligament is a thickening of the outer side of the capsule; it runs from the zygomatic arch to the neck of the mandible and prevents the condyle from moving backwards and downwards. The spheno- and stylomandibular ligaments are accessory ligaments away from the capsule.
